title: Apex Frozen Foods Ltd - 540692 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Apex Frozen Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 138% YoY to INR22 crores on 15% higher shrimp realisation (INR930/kg), despite 13% lower volumes at 2,624 MT.
summary.overview: Revenue was flat at INR257 crores against INR258 crores a year earlier, while EBITDA rose 79% to INR33 crores and margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%. Shrimp sales volume fell to 2,624 MT from 3,015 MT, hit by April-May labour shortages, container and equipment shortages, and EU shipment clearance delays that spilled into Q2. Management kept full-year production guidance at around 12,000 MT and said Q2 volume should recover, subject to global transport normalising. Realisation was guided to hold near INR900 per kg in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR258 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Accounted for 70% of shrimp sales in Q1 FY27 vs 54% a year earlier; sales rose 13% YoY and 121% QoQ. Pricing includes a 10% tariff plus ADD/CVD (about 9%).

segments.name: EU and UK
segments.commentary: Contributed 25% of shrimp sales vs 39% in Q1 FY26, hit by war-led transport disruption and origin-side testing and certification requirements; management said EU volumes spilled into Q2.

segments.name: Ready-to-Eat (RTE)
segments.commentary: 16% of Q1 volume vs 15% last year; management targets at least 18-20% of volume in FY27, with RTE margin about USD 0.50/kg above RTC at minimum.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 production guided at around 12,000 MT, reiterated from the start of the year; management said the earlier 14,000 MT figure was not a company guidance.
Q2 volume recovery expected, subject to global transport normalisation; order book covers sales until about mid-Q3 FY27.
Realisation in Q2 expected near INR900/kg, similar to Q1.
Margins expected to stay broadly stable, with partial pressure from higher ocean freight (more than doubled since Q4 FY26) and rising farm-gate prices.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 35-40% through FY27; next growth stage of 14,000-15,000 MT considered for FY28-29, not yet firmly committed.
Japan business initiated; Russia expected to start by end-Q2 or Q3 FY27; Australia still at audit stage.
capex_capacity: Volume capacity utilisation 38% in Q1 FY27 vs 39% in Q1 FY26; management targets sustained 35-40% through the year.
RTE capacity utilisation 16%, similar to prior year.
Labour shortage in April-May due to summer heat was resolved toward end-Q1 per management.
Raw material supply tightness expected to ease as new crop comes in.
No capex plans were announced in the call.
demand_pricing: Realisation of INR930/kg is up about INR80-90/kg YoY, helped by higher USD unit values, a weaker rupee and a higher RTE mix.
US buyers placed more orders after tariff uncertainty eased; the 10% tariff has been stable since the start of the year.
Farm-gate prices rose about 6-7% over the 3-4 weeks before the call; Q1 prices were described as stable.
Management said realisations above a certain level would hurt consumption and volumes, as in FY22-23.
UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How are fish meal and feed price increases affecting farmers and the company, and are they temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feed manufacturing is not part of the business. Farm-gate prices rising gave farmers comfort; margins should stay stable, with freight and farm-gate price increases as partial offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 12,000 MT. Q1 was hit by labour shortage and container shortages, and EU shipments slipped into Q2, which made US volumes look high. The order book is firm to mid-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?
qa_highlights.answer: RTE was 16% of Q1 volume and is expected to reach at least 18-20% in FY27. The margin premium is at least USD 0.50/kg over RTC, with some products higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ADD is at 3.4%, up from 1.35%, with a final determination around September 2026. CVD could fall by about 5.77% in December 2026 if duty drawback and RoDTEP are accepted as non-subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Proprietary customer-developed RTE and RTC products are already being shipped, estimated at 3-4% of sales (about 300-400 MT on 12,000 MT), rising to about 500 MT annually.

risks_watch: Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 because of war-led disruption; freight is the main risk to margin stability.
EU and UK volumes dropped to 25% of sales; watch whether shipments normalise in Q2 and whether testing or certification delays persist.
Full-year volume of about 12,000 MT requires roughly 9,000+ MT in the remaining three quarters versus 2,624 MT in Q1 FY27.
Capacity utilisation of 38% is well below the 14,000-15,000 MT next-stage ambition.
Possible US tariff refunds are unclear; the CVD review in December 2026 and the ADD determination in September 2026 could change pricing.
Farm-gate price increases and tight raw material supply could pressure costs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and pricing, but cautious and hedged on volumes, freight and the timing of FTA benefits. Management avoided committing to FY28-29 volume figures and said it was too early to say.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 was a quarter of mixed trends with improving global shrimp prices and higher conversion rate for USD INR, aiding realization growth on one hand, while labour shortage mainly in the months of April and May and war -led transportation disruptions across certain export markets affecting the shrimp sales volumes on the other hand.
We are hopeful of a recovery in sales volume in the Q2 of FY27, subject to the normalization or improvement of global transportation conditions.
So, for now, we have estimated the current year production to be around 12,000 metric tons.
Of course, ADD and CVD is part of our pricing.
But FY26, our overall sales increased. I mean, even though the U.S. was lower, but we diversified into other markets.

adds.what: Next capacity round of 14,000-15,000 MT (not yet firmly committed)

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue was flat at INR257 crores and shrimp volume fell 13% to 2,624 MT; FY27 output is held at ~12,000 MT with utilisation targeted at 35-40%, and the next 14,000-15,000 MT round is for FY28-29 and not firmly committed, so no near-term volume growth is backed.
